ei.title: 7번: How Tiny Organisms Changed the Atmosphere
ei.subject: 빠른독해바른독해_구문독해_2024

fullPassage: Around 2.35 billion years ago, Earth's atmosphere underwent a significant transition: It went from being oxygen-free to possessing a small percentage of oxygen. This change was partly due to tiny organisms known as cyanobacteria. Cyanobacteria, which evolved approximately 2.7 billion years ago, took in water to obtain hydrogen. This allowed them to assimilate carbon from CO₂ in the atmosphere. They then released oxygen as waste. But how could such tiny creatures have caused such a huge change in the planet? It is believed that the amount of oxygen cyanobacteria released slowly increased over hundreds of millions of years. Over this period, it accumulated in Earth's oceans, oxygenating the water. Eventually, the oceans' accumulated oxygen began to escape into the atmosphere. There, it reacted with methane, gradually displacing it. Had there been no cyanobacteria, oxygen might never have become a major component of Earth's atmosphere.

questions.passage: Around 2.35 billion years ago, Earth's atmosphere underwent a (A)[significant / minor] transition: It went from being oxygen-free to possessing a small percentage of oxygen. This change was partly due to tiny organisms known as cyanobacteria. Cyanobacteria, which evolved approximately 2.7 billion years ago, took in water to (B)[lose / obtain] hydrogen. This allowed them to assimilate carbon from CO₂ in the atmosphere. They then (C)[absorbed / released] oxygen as waste. But how could such tiny creatures have caused such a huge change in the planet? It is believed that the amount of oxygen cyanobacteria released slowly increased over hundreds of millions of years. Over this period, it accumulated in Earth's oceans, oxygenating the water. Eventually, the oceans' accumulated oxygen began to escape into the atmosphere. There, it reacted with methane, gradually displacing it. Had there been no cyanobacteria, oxygen might never have become a major component of Earth's atmosphere.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) significant=상당한 / minor=사소한 (B) obtain=얻다 / lose=잃다 (C) released=방출했다 / absorbed=흡수했다
det.analysis:
① minor—obtain—released: (A) 대기의 '상당한(significant)' 변화라 significant가 맞음
② significant—obtain—released: 상당한 변화 + 수소를 '얻기(obtain)' 위해 + 산소를 '방출(released)' ←정답
③ significant—lose—absorbed: (B)(C) 수소를 '얻는(obtain)' 것이고, 산소를 '방출(released)'함
④ minor—lose—absorbed: 세 자리 모두 문맥과 반대
det.tip: significant(상당한) 변화, obtain(얻다) 수소, released(방출) 산소

It is believed that the amount of oxygen cyanobacteria released slowly increased over hundreds of millions of years. There, it reacted with methane, gradually (C)[restoring / displacing] it. Had there been no cyanobacteria, oxygen might never have become a major component of Earth's atmosphere.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) accumulated=축적되었다 / scattered=흩어졌다 (B) escape=빠져나가다 / remain=남아 있다 (C) displacing=대체하며 / restoring=복원하며
det.analysis:
① accumulated—remain—restoring: (B) 산소가 대기로 '빠져나감(escape)'이 맞음
② scattered—escape—displacing: (A) 산소가 바다에 '축적되었다(accumulated)'가 맞음
③ accumulated—escape—displacing: 바다에 축적 + 대기로 빠져나감 + 메탄을 대체하며(displacing) ←정답
④ scattered—remain—restoring: 세 자리 모두 문맥과 반대
det.tip: accumulated(축적), escape(빠져나감), displacing(대체하며)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) evolved=진화했다 / vanished=사라졌다 (B) assimilate=흡수하다 / expel=배출하다 (C) increased=증가했다 / declined=감소했다
det.analysis:
① evolved—assimilate—increased: 남세균이 진화 + 탄소를 흡수(assimilate) + 산소량이 증가(increased) ←정답
② vanished—expel—increased: (A) 남세균이 '진화(evolved)'했고, (B) 탄소를 '흡수(assimilate)'함
③ evolved—expel—declined: (B)(C) 흡수(assimilate)하고 산소량이 '증가(increased)'함
④ vanished—assimilate—declined: (A)(C) 문맥과 반대
det.tip: evolved(진화), assimilate(흡수), increased(증가)

It is believed that the amount of oxygen cyanobacteria released slowly increased over hundreds of millions of years. Over this period, it ④<u>decreased</u> in Earth's oceans, oxygenating the water. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① transition=전환 ② evolved=진화했다 ③ waste=노폐물 ④ accumulated→decreased (부적절)
det.analysis:
① transition: 대기가 상당한 '전환(transition)'을 겪음 — 적절
② evolved: 남세균이 약 27억 년 전 '진화(evolved)'함 — 적절
③ waste: 산소를 '노폐물(waste)'로 방출함 — 적절
④ decreased: 산소가 바다에서 '감소했다(decreased)'? 이 시기에 산소가 바다에 '축적되어(accumulated)' 물에 산소를 공급했다가 원문 ←정답
det.tip: 산소가 바다에 accumulated(축적). decreased(감소)면 물에 산소 공급이 안 됨 → 모순

This change was partly due to tiny organisms known as cyanobacteria. Cyanobacteria, which evolved approximately 2.7 billion years ago, took in water to ②<u>obtain</u> hydrogen. This allowed them to ③<u>assimilate</u> carbon from CO₂ in the atmosphere. They then released oxygen as waste. But how could such tiny creatures have caused such a huge change in the planet? It is believed that the amount of oxygen cyanobacteria released slowly ④<u>increased</u> over hundreds of millions of years. Over this period, it accumulated in Earth's oceans, oxygenating the water. Eventually, the oceans' accumulated oxygen began to escape into the atmosphere. There, it reacted with methane, gradually displacing it. Had there been no cyanobacteria, oxygen might never have become a major component of Earth's atmosphere.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ①이 문맥상 부적절해요. 원문은 possessing(지니다)인데 lacking(없는)으로 바뀌었어요. ② obtain=얻다 ③ assimilate=흡수하다 ④ increased=증가했다
det.analysis:
① lacking: 무산소 상태에서 소량의 산소가 '없는(lacking)' 상태로 바뀜? 무산소에서 소량의 산소를 '지니는(possessing)' 상태로 바뀌었다가 원문 ←정답
② obtain: 물을 흡수해 수소를 '얻음(obtain)' — 적절
③ assimilate: 대기의 CO₂에서 탄소를 '흡수(assimilate)' — 적절
④ increased: 산소량이 서서히 '증가(increased)'함 — 적절
det.tip: 무산소 → 소량 산소를 possessing(지니는) 상태로 변화. lacking(없는)이면 변화가 없음

It is believed that the amount of oxygen cyanobacteria released slowly increased over hundreds of millions of years. Over this period, it accumulated in Earth's oceans, oxygenating the water. Eventually, the oceans' accumulated oxygen began to ②<u>sink</u> into the atmosphere. There, it reacted with methane, gradually ③<u>displacing</u> it. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① released=방출했다 ② escape→sink (부적절) ③ displacing=대체하며 ④ major=주요한
det.analysis:
① released: 산소를 노폐물로 '방출(released)'함 — 적절
② sink: 바다에 축적된 산소가 대기로 '가라앉기(sink)' 시작? 대기로 '빠져나가기(escape)' 시작했다가 원문이며, 가라앉는 것은 위로 올라가는 대기와 모순 ←정답
③ displacing: 산소가 메탄을 점차 '대체하며(displacing)' — 적절
④ major: 산소가 대기의 '주요한(major)' 구성 요소가 됨 — 적절
det.tip: 바다의 산소가 대기로 escape(빠져나감). sink(가라앉다)는 방향이 정반대

det.korean: carbon=탄소 / nitrogen=질소 / hydrogen=수소 / sunlight=햇빛
det.analysis:

det.tip: released(방출)의 반대는 absorbed(흡수). emitted(배출)는 유사어 함정, evolved·obtained는 의미축이 다른 오답

questions.passage:
(A) Around 2.35 billion years ago, Earth's atmosphere underwent a major <u>change</u>, going from being oxygen-free to containing oxygen.

(B) I searched all my pockets for coins, but I didn't have enough <u>change</u> to pay for the bus ticket.
questions.stem: 다음 (A)와 (B)에서 밑줄 친 change의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: change: (A) 변화 (B) (동전 등의) 잔돈
det.analysis:
① (A) 변화 (B) 잔돈: 대기가 겪은 '변화(change)', 버스비를 낼 '잔돈(change)' ←정답
② (A) 잔돈 (B) 변화: (A) 대기가 겪은 것은 잔돈이 아니라 변화
③ (A) 변화 (B) 거스름돈을 주다: (B) 여기서는 동사가 아니라 '잔돈'이라는 명사
④ (A) 교환 (B) 잔돈: (A) 무산소→산소는 상태의 '변화'이지 교환이 아님
det.tip: change의 다의어: (상태의) 변화 vs (동전) 잔돈

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "to gradually collect and increase in quantity over a period of time"

det.korean: release=방출하다 / escape=빠져나가다 / accumulate=축적하다 / obtain=얻다
det.analysis:
① release: 방출하다 — 밖으로 내보낸다는 뜻이라 정의와 반대
② escape: 빠져나가다 — 정의와 무관
③ accumulate: 오랜 시간에 걸쳐 점차 모여 양이 늘어나는 것 ←정답
④ obtain: 얻다 — 한 번 획득한다는 뜻으로 '점차 축적'과 다름
det.tip: gradually collect and increase over time(점차 모여 늘어남) → accumulate(축적하다)

questions.passage: This change was partly due to tiny organisms __________ (know) as cyanobacteria. Cyanobacteria, which evolved approximately 2.7 billion years ago, took in water to obtain hydrogen.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: know(알다) → known (과거분사). organisms __ as ~ = ~로 알려진 유기체 (수동 관계)
det.analysis: know를 known으로 바꿔요. 'tiny organisms known as cyanobacteria'는 '남세균으로 알려진 작은 유기체'라는 뜻이에요. 유기체(organisms)는 그렇게 '알려지는' 대상이라, 명사를 뒤에서 꾸미는 과거분사 known(~로 알려진)이 필요해요.
det.tip: 명사 + known as ~ = ~로 알려진 (과거분사가 명사 수식)

questions.passage: Around 2.35 billion years ago, Earth's atmosphere underwent a significant transition. It went from being oxygen-free to __________ (possess) a small percentage of oxygen.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: possess(지니다) → possessing (동명사). from being ~ to ___ing = ~에서 …하는 것으로 (전치사 to 뒤 동명사)
det.analysis: possess를 possessing으로 바꿔요. 'went from being oxygen-free to possessing ~'은 'from A to B(A에서 B로)' 구조인데, 앞의 being과 짝을 이루도록 to 뒤에도 동명사가 와야 해요. 여기서 to는 to부정사가 아니라 전치사라, 그 뒤에는 동명사 possessing이 필요해요.
det.tip: from being ~ to + 동명사(-ing). to가 전치사라 뒤에 possessing

questions.passage: Around 2.35 billion years ago, Earth's atmosphere underwent a significant transition: It went from being oxygen-free to possessing a small percentage of oxygen. This change was partly due to tiny organisms known as cyanobacteria. Cyanobacteria, which evolved approximately 2.7 billion years ago, took in water to obtain hydrogen. This allowed them to assimilate carbon from CO₂ in the atmosphere. They then released oxygen as waste. But how could such tiny creatures have caused such a huge change in the planet? It is believed that the amount of oxygen cyanobacteria released slowly increased over hundreds of millions of years. Over this period, it accumulated in Earth's oceans, oxygenating the water. Eventually, the oceans' accumulated oxygen began to __________. There, it reacted with methane, gradually displacing it. Had there been no cyanobacteria, oxygen might never have become a major component of Earth's atmosphere.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: escape into the atmosphere=대기로 빠져나가다 / sink into the oceans=바다로 가라앉다 / react with hydrogen=수소와 반응하다 / disappear from the Earth=지구에서 사라지다
det.analysis:
① escape into the atmosphere: 바다에 축적된 산소가 마침내 '대기로 빠져나가기' 시작 = 뒤 문장 'There(거기서), 메탄과 반응'과 이어짐 ←정답
② sink into the oceans: 산소는 이미 바다에 있었으므로 다시 바다로 가라앉는다는 것은 모순
③ react with hydrogen: 수소와의 반응은 본문에 없음
④ disappear from the Earth: 사라지는 것이 아니라 대기의 주요 성분이 됨
det.tip: 뒤 문장 There, it reacted with methane(거기서 메탄과 반응) → 산소가 대기로 escape

questions.passage: Around 2.35 billion years ago, Earth's atmosphere underwent a significant transition: It went from being oxygen-free to possessing a small percentage of oxygen. This change was partly due to tiny organisms known as cyanobacteria. Cyanobacteria, which evolved approximately 2.7 billion years ago, took in water to obtain hydrogen. This allowed them to __________ from CO₂ in the atmosphere. They then released oxygen as waste. But how could such tiny creatures have caused such a huge change in the planet? It is believed that the amount of oxygen cyanobacteria released slowly increased over hundreds of millions of years. Over this period, it accumulated in Earth's oceans, oxygenating the water. Eventually, the oceans' accumulated oxygen began to escape into the atmosphere. There, it reacted with methane, gradually displacing it. Had there been no cyanobacteria, oxygen might never have become a major component of Earth's atmosphere.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: release oxygen=산소를 방출하다 / obtain hydrogen=수소를 얻다 / break down water=물을 분해하다 / assimilate carbon=탄소를 흡수하다
det.analysis:
① release oxygen: 산소 방출은 그다음(then) 단계로 뒤에 따로 나옴
② obtain hydrogen: 수소를 얻는 것은 앞 문장(물을 흡수해)에서 이미 일어난 일
③ break down water: 물을 분해한다는 표현은 본문에 없음
④ assimilate carbon: 수소를 얻은 덕분에 대기의 CO₂에서 '탄소를 흡수함' ←정답
det.tip: This allowed them to ___ from CO₂(CO₂로부터) → assimilate carbon(탄소를 흡수)
